public_rationale: The reviewed evidence includes major capability progress, but no decisive demonstration of LLM-only AGI. The independent benchmark evaluator expressly declines to make that claim. This leaves Marcus's forecast open; it does not support the stronger assertion that LLMs will never reach AGI.
limitations: AGI and LLM-only systems have disputed boundaries.
The search cannot establish that every possible candidate or unpublished result has been examined.
Current limitations cannot prove an indefinite negative forecast.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are not AGI and will never become AGI on their own.

statement.excerpt: LLMs are not AGI, and (on their own) never will be; scaling alone was never going to be enough.
statement.document_title: The Great AI Retrenchment has begun

our_interpretation: AGI means broad human-level cognitive competence, including learning unfamiliar tasks, rather than success on one benchmark.
On their own restricts the system being evaluated: an LLM cannot rely on separate tools or cognitive machinery to supply the capabilities needed to qualify.
This is a scope restriction, not a conditional forecast awaiting an antecedent.
The present-tense clause and the indefinite future claim are assessed together. Evidence of present limitations cannot establish never.
criteria.support_condition: A validated general limitation establishes that LLMs within the stated scope cannot attain broad human-level cognitive competence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent evaluations establish broad human-level cognitive competence in an LLM alone, with sufficient technical disclosure to establish that the qualifying capabilities do not depend on excluded machinery.

evidence.explanation: The evaluator reports substantial progress but explicitly declines to establish AGI. This does not meet the early contradiction rule or establish permanent impossibility.
This review finds the published evidence insufficient to establish a prominent recent AGI claim. Its judgment concerns available evidence, not whether future LLMs could reach AGI.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independently replicated demonstration of broad human-level competence from an LLM alone, with sufficient technical disclosure, or a validated general impossibility result covering that system class.
